chunks: Justice puts things in their places, while generosity takes them out from their direction; justice is the general caretaker, while generosity is a particular benefit; therefore, justice is more noble and superior of the two.

key_terms.أَشْرَفُهُمَا: The more noble of the two

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between justice and generosity according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali distinguishes between justice as a universal, structural principle that maintains cosmic and social order, and generosity as a transient, individual virtue. Shia scholars emphasize that while generosity is praiseworthy, justice is superior because it is the foundational attribute of God and the prophets, ensuring equity for all rather than favoring the few. This hierarchy reflects the Shia theological view that 'Adl is one of the five pillars of Usul al-Din, essential for the establishment of divine law.
